newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks gain one pct, hit 15th record close.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks gain one pct, hit 15th record close.

* Toronto's key stock index climbed one percent on Monday to post the year's 15th record close, rallying on stronger banks.
* Trading was light at 60.3 million shares worth C$872.7 million.
Toronto stocks extended last week's gains for their third straight record close on Monday and 15th of this year, on the back of stronger bank issues.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index climbed 69.62 points to 6491.13.
Trading was light at 60.3 million shares valued at C$872.7 million, as markets in New York and London were closed for holidays.
The weighty bank sector of Canada's largest equities market gained 2.3 percent ahead of quarterly profit reports starting on Tuesday.

Investors bought Canadian issues on Monday because they looked inexpensive compared to U.S. stocks after Friday when Wall Street posted its 20th record finish of the year, Montreal-based strategist Bill Ram said.
"Overall, what we're doing is a little bit of catch-up with New York," he said.
All of Toronto's 14 sub-groups rose, led by consumer products, banks, conglomerates and media.
Advancing stocks outnumbered decliners 553 to 390, while 306 ended steady.
Analysts expected Canada's big six banks to post record profits for the fourth consecutive quarter, starting with Bank of Montreal and Bank of Nova Scotia on Tuesday.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Royal Bank of Canada, the nation's largest, led the banks' upward march, gaining 1.65 to 61.70, followed by Bank of Nova Scotia, which jumped 1.25 to 58.80.
* Toronto-based Rex Diamond Mining Corp dropped 0.70 to 2.85 in active trading.
